newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse head sees faster expansion in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse head sees faster expansion in 1997.

text.p: Next year's flotations of some of Poland's largest firms and the listing of its mass privatisation funds will speed up the Warsaw bourse's growth and lure new foreign investors, the exchange's head said on Thursday.

Wieslaw Rozlucki, speaking at a conference on investment opportunities, said that even though the bourse's capitalisation was likely to double this year, it was still too low at the current 25 billion zlotys or nine percent of GDP.
"I think it is an absolute minimum for the bourse to have 20 percent of GDP and this shows that we have to grow faster," Rozlucki said.
"Next year I expect the market capitalisation to be boosted by the privatisation of the KGHM (Polska Miedz copper concern) and Bank Handlowy," he added.

He said he hoped shares of the 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs), which run more than 500 companies privatised under Poland's mass privatisation scheme, would hit the bourse in the first quarter of next year as originally planned.
He also said he expected first of the individual firms in the programme to start trading on the Warsaw exchange before the end of this year.

He said the expansion should help attract foreign investors in particular, who now hold about 25 percent share of the market and have pointed to the market's relative small size as the main barrier to larger investment.

"I have been hearing from foreign investors that they would like to come to Poland but that there is not enough to buy, so my message is: keep your wallets ready becasue the supply is coming," Rozlucki said.

Asked whether the Polish market would be able to digest offerings of such heavyweights as KGHM, Bank Handlowy or the telecom monopolist TPSA or Plock refinery, which might come to the market later on, Rozlucki said:
"I think the method for big privatisations such as KGHM or Handlowy will be to start with small tranches of shares that the market will easily absorb."
